faq.q: What is the origin of Aisha?
faq.a: Aisha is associated with Arabic. Variant romanization of عائشة. The source record left this name with no origin and no script form.
Yes — the underlying form عائشة is Arabic.
Aisha can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Aisha should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. عائشة is not a Qur'anic form; it is the name of ʿĀʾisha bint Abī Bakr in the hadith and sīra tradition

faq.q: What does Aisha mean in Urdu?

faq.q: What are the variants of Aisha?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Aisha, aisha. Script forms are عائشة, عائشہ, عايشه, आइशा.

faq.q: Is Aisha a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
